recommended.title: Insta360 Ace Pro FPV Test: HDR and PureVideo at Sunset
recommended.description:
I mounted an Insta360 Ace Pro on an FPV quad for a first-flight field test at sunset. This video shows the improvised mount, a 4K30 Active HDR flight, a 4K30 PureVideo flight as the light falls, and the questions I still had afterward.

This is hands-on first-flight footage, not a controlled camera comparison or final review. The original session did not preserve every setting clearly enough for me to claim an exact stabilization, sharpness, color-profile, or raw-versus-edited comparison. I would lock those variables before repeating the test.

Chapters:
0:00 Test plan and improvised mount
0:31 Golden-hour setup
1:10 Ace Pro recording-mode overview
2:25 Battery and mount check
3:18 4K30 Active HDR flight
5:18 PureVideo after sunset
6:57 What I still wanted to test
7:12 Second low-light flight
9:34 Field-test takeaway

pinnedComment.text:
Transparency note: this was my first field flight with the Ace Pro, not a controlled comparison. The original session did not preserve every setting clearly enough for me to claim an exact stabilization, sharpness, color-profile, or raw-versus-edited test.

The most useful questions here are still the ones viewers raised: exact settings, low-light behavior, stabilization, and weight. If I repeat this test with every variable locked, which two modes should I compare first?

commentReplies.text: Good question. I did not preserve enough of the original session settings to give you a reliable exact answer, so I do not want to guess. A repeat test should show the full settings screen, raw clip, export settings, and mounted weight together.

The weight tradeoff was real in this first flight. I have not documented a safe battery-free external-power setup for this exact rig, so I would treat that as a new test rather than advice from this upload.
